messages:
morgan: quick heads-up — noticed a perf regression on prod canary when we flip to fused-flash on seq_len=2048. ~9% p99 increase for generation heavy tails. link: https://ci.example/rt/prof/2109876 :eyes:

kai: can you paste the flame? is it KV eviction or kernel stalls? :thinking:

morgan: flame shows lots of stall time inside kv_read for interleaved layout + odd stride patterns. cpu/gpu overlap looks fine. suspect set-assoc thrashing when some sequences have long prefixes.

sasha: hmm. is the regression only with fused-flash or also with paged-attention?

morgan: only fused-flash variant + interleaved kv. paged and separate-kv look stable.

anna: idea: try a set-associative bucketing for interleaved KV rather than pure linear interleave. reduces conflict misses when strides align badly.

sasha: agree. also try force-aligned base pointer (pad 64 bytes) and verify dtype downcast path. we've seen misaligned bf16 reads cost more on Ampere kernels.

kai: can we microbench a tiny harness? zach, can you run a quick bench script that toggles layout and stride pad?

zach: on it. will run kbench with these variants:

```
./kbench --model tiny-2048 --mode fused-flash --layout interleaved --assoc 1 --pad 0
./kbench --model tiny-2048 --mode fused-flash --layout interleaved --assoc 4 --pad 64
./kbench --model tiny-2048 --mode fused-flash --layout separate --pad 64
```

zach: posting initial numbers: interleaved assoc=1 pad=0 -> 810 tokens/s; assoc=4 pad=64 -> 930 tokens/s; separate pad=64 -> 950 tokens/s. so assoc helps but separate still best.

morgan: good signal. can you also capture kv_access trace and bucket hit/miss counters?

zach: yes adding metrics: bucket_hits, bucket_evictions, bank_conflicts per-step. will upload.

perf-bot: perf artifact uploaded: https://ci.example/artifacts/2109876/kbench-report.json

anna: downstream implication: our automatic kernel selector currently prefers fused-flash when memory layout == interleaved. maybe selector should score by predicted bucket_conflict_rate for request seq length distribution.

sasha: +1. also add a heuristic: if bucket_evictions per 1k tokens > threshold, fallback to paged-attention or separate-kv kernel.

kai: for rollout, propose canary on dedicated pool with traffic shaped to heavy-tail prompts. if metrics stable for 24h, promote. otherwise auto-fallback.

morgan: I'll open a tiny RFC to change selector scoring and add the eviction-based fallback. aim for canary tomorrow.

sasha: include config knobs: assoc_buckets, bucket_size, pad_bytes, eviction_threshold. sample config: 

```
kv_layout_config = {
  "mode": "set-assoc",
  "assoc_buckets": "4",
  "bucket_size": "256",
  "pad_bytes": "64",
  "dtype": "bfloat16"
}
```

anna: also consider batching heuristic: group requests by prefix length to reduce mixed-stride batches (batching currently mixes short+long -> more cross-bank pressure).

kai: good point. adjust batcher: prefer homogeneous prefix-length windowing when latency budget allows. small window parameter: prefix_window_ms=20.

zach: will add experiments. running the new batcher with assoc=4 now.

morgan: thanks all. action items: zach run extended kbench + traces, kai update selector scoring PR, sasha add fallback rule, anna prototype batch-windowing. I'll schedule canary once zach uploads 24h artifact. :rocket:
